title.en: Bound to, likely to, chances are

es: Reconocer y graduar la probabilidad con bound to, likely to, chances are, there is a good chance y may well.

teaching.en: Our team is bound to win on Saturday because it has not lost a match this year.
teaching.es: Nuestro equipo seguro que gana el sábado porque no ha perdido ningún partido este año.
teaching.explanationEs: Be bound to + verbo base: casi seguro. No es una obligación, es certeza.
segments: Our team is bound to win on Saturday because
it has not lost a match this year.
teaching.audioText: Our team is bound to win on Saturday because it has not lost a match this year.

teaching.en: Leo is likely to score, because he is the best player in the team.
teaching.es: Es probable que Leo marque, porque es el mejor jugador del equipo.
teaching.explanationEs: Be likely to + verbo base: probable, más posible que no.
segments: Leo is likely to score, because he
is the best player in the team.
teaching.audioText: Leo is likely to score, because he is the best player in the team.

teaching.en: Chances are that the match will start late because of the rain.
teaching.es: Lo más probable es que el partido empiece tarde por la lluvia.
teaching.explanationEs: Chances are (that) + frase completa con sujeto y verbo.
segments: Chances are that the match will
start late because of the rain.
teaching.audioText: Chances are that the match will start late because of the rain.

teaching.en: There is a good chance that Sara will play on Saturday.
teaching.es: Hay buenas posibilidades de que Sara juegue el sábado.
teaching.explanationEs: There is a good chance (that) + frase: buena posibilidad, sin asegurarla.
segments: There is a good chance that
Sara will play on Saturday.
teaching.audioText: There is a good chance that Sara will play on Saturday.

teaching.en: The other team may well be stronger, so nobody can be sure.
teaching.es: Bien puede que el otro equipo sea más fuerte, así que nadie puede estar seguro.
teaching.explanationEs: May well + verbo base: es bastante posible; sube la fuerza de may.
segments: The other team may well be
stronger, so nobody can be sure.
teaching.audioText: The other team may well be stronger, so nobody can be sure.

teaching.en: Tom is unlikely to play because he hurt his leg last week.
teaching.es: Es improbable que Tom juegue porque se lesionó la pierna la semana pasada.
teaching.explanationEs: Be unlikely to + verbo base: poco probable.
segments: Tom is unlikely to play because
he hurt his leg last week.
teaching.audioText: Tom is unlikely to play because he hurt his leg last week.

prompt.es: Según el texto, ¿qué se dice de Hill?

choices.text: Hill is likely to finish second.
Hill is bound to finish second.
Hill is unlikely to finish second.

feedback.es: El texto dice que Hill «is only likely to finish second»: es probable, pero no seguro. Bound to sería certeza.

hint.es: Busca la expresión que lleva only: es probable, no casi seguro.

origin.text: Two teams, two predictions. Riverside has won every match this year, so it is bound to win on Saturday. Hill has a new coach, so it is only likely to finish second.

accepted: unlikely

hint.es: La lesión hace que jugar sea poco probable, no probable.

title.en: Must have been doing, might have been taken
title.es: Estaría haciéndolo o se lo llevaron

es: Formar must / might / can't have been + -ing y must / might / can't have been + participio para especular sobre procesos y hechos pasivos del pasado.

teaching.en: Our neighbour must have been sleeping, because he did not hear the noise.
teaching.es: Nuestro vecino debía de estar durmiendo, porque no oyó el ruido.
teaching.explanationEs: Must have been + -ing: casi seguro de una acción que estaba en curso.
segments: Our neighbour must have been sleeping, because
he did not hear the noise.
teaching.audioText: Our neighbour must have been sleeping, because he did not hear the noise.

teaching.en: A guest might have been using the kitchen, because the light was on.
teaching.es: Puede que un invitado estuviera usando la cocina, porque la luz estaba encendida.
teaching.explanationEs: Might have been + -ing: posible, sin certeza.
segments: A guest might have been using the
kitchen, because the light was on.
teaching.audioText: A guest might have been using the kitchen, because the light was on.

teaching.en: Mia can't have been cooking all day, because the cake came from the shop.
teaching.es: Mia no puede haber estado cocinando todo el día, porque la tarta es de la tienda.
teaching.explanationEs: Can't have been + -ing: seguro que no ocurrió.
segments: Mia can't have been cooking all day,
because the cake came from the shop.
teaching.audioText: Mia can't have been cooking all day, because the cake came from the shop.

teaching.en: The cake might have been taken by the dog.
teaching.es: Puede que el perro se llevara la tarta.
teaching.explanationEs: Might have been + participio: hipótesis sobre lo que le pasó a algo (voz pasiva).
segments: The cake might have been
taken by the dog.
teaching.audioText: The cake might have been taken by the dog.

teaching.en: Mia's costume must have been stolen, because it is not in her room.
teaching.es: El disfraz de Mia debe de haber sido robado, porque no está en su habitación.
teaching.explanationEs: Must have been + participio: casi seguro de que alguien le hizo algo.
segments: Mia's costume must have been stolen, because
it is not in her room.
teaching.audioText: Mia's costume must have been stolen, because it is not in her room.

teaching.en: The party can't have been cancelled, because a guest is at the door.
teaching.es: La fiesta no puede haber sido cancelada, porque hay un invitado en la puerta.
teaching.explanationEs: Can't have been + participio: seguro que no le pasó eso.
segments: The party can't have been cancelled, because
a guest is at the door.
teaching.audioText: The party can't have been cancelled, because a guest is at the door.

prompt.es: Nadie abre la puerta. ¿Qué frase dice que Tom casi seguro estaba durmiendo?

choices.text: Tom can't have been sleeping.
Tom must have been sleeping.
Tom might have been sleeping.

feedback.es: Casi seguro se expresa con must. Can't diría que es imposible y might solo que es posible.

hint.es: Casi seguro se expresa con el modal más fuerte.

prompt.es: Completa: «Un invitado debió de estar en el baño, porque la puerta estaba cerrada.»

answer.text: been
accepted: been

feedback.es: La forma continua en pasado lleva have been + -ing: must have been using.

hint.es: Entre have y -ing va la palabra que une las dos formas.

origin.text: A guest must have ___ using the bathroom, because the door was closed.

prompt.es: Completa: «Puede que las invitaciones se enviaran a la dirección equivocada.»

answer.text: sent
accepted: sent

feedback.es: En pasiva, been va seguido del participio. El participio de send es sent.

hint.es: El participio de send es irregular.

origin.text: The invitations might have been ___ to the wrong address.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Los invitados no pueden haber estado bailando sin música.»

answer.text: The guests can't have been dancing without music
accepted: The guests can't have been dancing without music
Without music the guests can't have been dancing

feedback.es: Sujeto + can't have been + -ing: la deducción negativa sobre una acción que estaba en curso.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué deduce quien habla sobre el vecino.

choices.text: The neighbour was certainly not at home.
The neighbour might have been cooking.
The neighbour was almost certainly watching TV.

feedback.es: «Must have been watching» expresa casi certeza, apoyada en que se oía la tele a través de la pared.

origin.audio: The neighbour must have been watching TV, because we could hear it through the wall.

might have been sleeping
can't have been sleeping
might have been stolen

feedback.es: Cada modal da un grado: must es casi seguro, might es posible y can't es imposible. El par con stolen usa la pasiva: algo le pasó al sujeto.

pairs: must have been sleeping
might have been sleeping
can't have been sleeping
might have been stolen

prompt.es: Ana no encuentra su abrigo y cree que casi seguro se lo llevaron. ¿Qué frase lo dice?

title.en: What went wrong in the final?

es: Seguir comentarios que especulan sobre causas y distinguir certeza, probabilidad y duda.

teaching.en: The commentator said the goalkeeper must have been injured, because he did not move.
teaching.es: El comentarista dijo que el portero debió de lesionarse, porque no se movió.
teaching.explanationEs: Must have + participio: casi seguro; la pista va tras because.

teaching.audioText: The commentator said the goalkeeper must have been injured, because he did not move.

teaching.en: The defence may well have been tired after extra time.
teaching.es: Bien puede que la defensa estuviera cansada tras la prórroga.
teaching.explanationEs: May well have + participio: probable, más fuerte que might.
segments: The defence may well have
been tired after extra time.
teaching.audioText: The defence may well have been tired after extra time.

teaching.en: The referee can't have been the cause of our loss, because he was fair all through the match.
teaching.es: El árbitro no puede haber sido la causa de nuestra derrota, porque fue justo durante todo el partido.
teaching.explanationEs: Can't have + participio: seguro que no fue así.
segments: The referee can't have been the cause of our
loss, because he was fair all through the match.
teaching.audioText: The referee can't have been the cause of our loss, because he was fair all through the match.

teaching.en: It might have been bad luck, so nobody is to blame.
teaching.es: Puede que fuera mala suerte, así que nadie tiene la culpa.
teaching.explanationEs: Might have + participio: posible, sin certeza; is to blame = tiene la culpa.
segments: It might have been bad luck,
so nobody is to blame.
teaching.audioText: It might have been bad luck, so nobody is to blame.

teaching.en: The final was close, so one mistake could have changed the result.
teaching.es: La final estuvo reñida, así que un solo error pudo cambiar el resultado.
teaching.explanationEs: Could have + participio: algo que fue posible.
segments: The final was close, so one
mistake could have changed the result.
teaching.audioText: The final was close, so one mistake could have changed the result.

prompt.es: Según el texto, ¿qué causa ve Carlos como casi segura?

choices.text: The heat was too strong.
The other player was better.
Mia was nervous.

feedback.es: Carlos usa «must have been nervous»: casi seguro. El calor lo menciona Sara y Tom descarta que la otra jugadora fuera mejor.

hint.es: Busca must have: es la expresión más segura.

hint.es: May well no significa seguro: significa «bien puede que».

es: Exponer una teoría con pistas y dos grados de certeza distintos usando modales de deducción.

teaching.en: My theory is that someone must have been using the old library at night.
teaching.es: Mi teoría es que alguien debió de estar usando la biblioteca vieja por la noche.
teaching.explanationEs: My theory is that + frase: presenta lo que piensas; must have been marca certeza alta.
segments: My theory is that someone must have
been using the old library at night.
teaching.audioText: My theory is that someone must have been using the old library at night.

teaching.en: One clue is that there are footprints on the floor, so someone must have been inside.
teaching.es: Una pista es que hay huellas en el suelo, así que alguien debió de estar dentro.
teaching.explanationEs: La pista es un hecho que se ve; so lleva de la pista a la conclusión.
segments: One clue is that there are footprints on
the floor, so someone must have been inside.
teaching.audioText: One clue is that there are footprints on the floor, so someone must have been inside.

teaching.en: The evidence suggests that someone opened the window from the inside.
teaching.es: Las pruebas sugieren que alguien abrió la ventana desde dentro.
teaching.explanationEs: The evidence suggests that + frase: la prueba apunta a una idea, sin asegurarla del todo.
segments: The evidence suggests that someone opened
the window from the inside.
teaching.audioText: The evidence suggests that someone opened the window from the inside.

teaching.en: That would explain why the lights are on every night.
teaching.es: Eso explicaría por qué las luces están encendidas cada noche.
teaching.explanationEs: That would explain why + hecho: une una idea con lo que quieres explicar.
segments: That would explain why the
lights are on every night.
teaching.audioText: That would explain why the lights are on every night.

teaching.en: The mystery is not solved, but chances are that a student found a way in.
teaching.es: El misterio no está resuelto, pero lo más probable es que un estudiante encontrara la forma de entrar.
teaching.explanationEs: Chances are that + frase: un grado suave de certeza.
segments: The mystery is not solved, but chances are
that a student found a way in.
teaching.audioText: The mystery is not solved, but chances are that a student found a way in.

teaching.en: It can't have been the caretaker; he was at the match, and that is strong evidence.
teaching.es: No puede haber sido el conserje; estaba en el partido, y eso es una prueba sólida.
teaching.explanationEs: Can't have been + persona: descarta una posibilidad con una razón.
segments: It can't have been the caretaker; he was
at the match, and that is strong evidence.
teaching.audioText: It can't have been the caretaker; he was at the match, and that is strong evidence.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase da una pista (un hecho) y no una teoría?

choices.text: There is a red bag on the desk.
Someone must have climbed in.
